title: Marked cancellation triangle is anodyne
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns and Kan complexes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A marked simplicial set is a simplicial set with a subset of its edges containing all degenerate edges; maps preserve that subset. Write $K^\flat$ for marking only degenerate edges and $K^\sharp$ for marking all edges. Let $W$ be the smallest class of marked maps containing isomorphisms and closed under pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts, containing the following maps: $(\Lambda_i^n)^\flat\to(\Delta^n)^\flat$ for $0<i<n$; $(\Lambda_n^n,E\cap(\Lambda_n^n)_1)\to(\Delta^n,E)$ for $n>0$, where $E$ is the degenerate edges together with $[n-1,n]$; $(\Lambda_1^2)^\sharp\amalg_{(\Lambda_1^2)^\flat}(\Delta^2)^\flat\to(\Delta^2)^\sharp$; and $K^\flat\to K^\sharp$ for every Kan complex $K$. Here a small transfinite composition is a composite along a small ordinal, with colimits at limit stages, and a retract is a retract in the category of arrows. Then the identity on the underlying two-simplex
$$ (\Delta^2,\{\text{degenerate edges},[0,2],[1,2]\})\longrightarrow(\Delta^2)^\sharp $$
belongs to $W$.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.1.7 (the map obtained by marking the remaining edge [0,1]). Read online 2026-10-17; not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial result.

proof.text: Write $A=(\Delta^2,\{\text{degenerate edges},[0,2],[1,2]\})$, $B=(\Delta^2)^\sharp$, and $i:A\to B$. First replace the Kan generators in the definition of $W$ by a small set: take one representative of each countable Kan complex, together with the finite generators (i)--(iii), and call the resulting set $J$. Every edge of any small Kan complex $K$ lies in a countable Kan subcomplex. Indeed, start with that edge and its faces and degeneracies, and repeatedly add one filler in $K$ for each horn in the current countable subcomplex, including all faces and degeneracies of the chosen fillers. There are countably many horns at each stage. The union after countably many stages is Kan because a horn has finitely many nondegenerate simplices and therefore occurs at some finite stage. Well-order the edges of $K$ and, for each edge, push out the countable Kan marking generator for such a subcomplex along its inclusion into $K$ with the markings already added. Each pushout keeps the underlying simplicial set $K$ and adds the images of those marked edges. The resulting transfinite composite is $K^\flat\to K^\sharp$. Thus $J$ generates exactly $W$. In particular, lifting against $J$ implies lifting against every generator in the statement: lifts extend across a pushout by its universal property, across a continuous transfinite chain by successive compatible lifts, and across a retract by the retraction maps.

source.place: Remark 3.1.1.3; explicit countable Kan-subcomplex and marking-pushout argument.

proof.text: In the category of small marked simplicial sets, small colimits are degreewise simplicial colimits with the marked edges the images of marked edges of the inputs. This follows directly by testing whether the induced maps preserve marked edges; degenerate edges are included automatically. Hom sets and all these colimits lie in the fixed universe. Every map of $J$ is degreewise injective, and its domain has countably many simplices. In a continuous $\aleph_1$-chain of pushouts of coproducts of $J$-maps, a map from such a domain factors through one stage: bound the countably many stages at which its simplices and required marked edges appear. The regularity of $\aleph_1$ gives a bound below $\aleph_1$; the same argument detects equality of two maps. These are exactly the smallness hypotheses of [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization], with $I=J$ and $\kappa=\aleph_1$. It factors $i$ as $A\xrightarrow{j} Z\xrightarrow{p}B$, with $j$ a $J$-cell map and $p$ lifting against $J$. A coproduct attachment can be serialized by well-ordering its summands, so $j\in W$. Step 1 makes $p$ lift every marked generator. Generator (i) therefore makes $p$ an inner fibration; generator (ii), for $n\geq2$, makes every marked edge $p$-cartesian in the horn sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Its $n=1$ case supplies a marked lift with specified target of every base edge. The underlying $B=\Delta^2$ is a quasicategory: compatible inner horns in the nerve of the linear order $[2]$ extend to the corresponding nondecreasing chain. Consequently $Z$ is a quasicategory too, by filling the image inner horn in $B$ and lifting that filler through $p$.

source.place: Remark 3.1.1.3, Proposition A.1.2.5; proof of Proposition 3.1.1.6, conditions (A), (C), and marked implies cartesian.

proof.text: Let $\sigma:\Delta^2\to Z$ be the underlying map of $j$, and write $f=\sigma_{01}$, $g=\sigma_{12}$ and $h=\sigma_{02}$. The edges $g,h$ are marked, hence $p$-cartesian by Step 2. Apply the composition clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] to $p^{\mathrm{op}}:Z^{\mathrm{op}}\to B^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\sigma^{\mathrm{op}}$. Opposite reverses the vertex order and sends an $n$-horn of index $r$ to the horn of index $n-r$; thus the horn definition in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] identifies $p$-cartesian edges with $p^{\mathrm{op}}$-cocartesian edges. Both opposite simplicial sets are quasicategories and $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ is inner, by this same reversal of inner horns. The first consecutive edge in $\sigma^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $g^{\mathrm{op}}$, the second is $f^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the long edge is $h^{\mathrm{op}}$. Since the first and long edges are cocartesian, the cited equivalence makes the second cocartesian. Hence $f$ is $p$-cartesian.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.1.7 and Proposition 2.4.1.7, expressed by the existing opposite-variance composition lemma.

proof.text: Choose a marked edge $f':z'_0\to z_1$ over $[0,1]$ with target $z_1=\sigma(1)$, using the $n=1$ marked-generator lift of Step 2. There is a triangle $\tau$ with $d_0\tau=f'$, $d_1\tau=f$ and $p\tau=s_0[0,1]$: solve the type-(ii) $n=2$ horn whose edges $[0,2]$ and $[1,2]$ are $f,f'$ and whose base vertices are $(0,0,1)$. Its required marked final edge is $f'$, so this is an allowed marked lifting problem. Put $a=d_2\tau:z_0\to z'_0$. The two edges $f,f'$ are $p$-cartesian. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] to the opposite of this triangle, exactly as in Step 3: $f'$ is the last consecutive edge before reversal and $f$ is the long edge, so $a$ is $p$-cartesian. The edge $a$ lies in $F=Z\times_B\{0\}$. The fiber $F$ is a quasicategory, since its inner horns lift against $p$ over the constant simplex at $0$. Every final outer horn in $F$ ending in $a$ fills in $F$: use the $p$-cartesian horn condition of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] over the constant base simplex. By the converse outer-horn criterion of [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling], $a$ is an equivalence in $F$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.1.1.6, the cartesian implies marked argument in (B); Proposition 2.4.1.7 and Proposition 1.2.4.3.

proof.text: The structure map $F\to\Delta^0$ is an isofibration in the sense of [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration]: $F$ is a quasicategory by Step 4, so inner horns lift, and the only edge of $\Delta^0$ is degenerate and lifts at any $c$ to the degenerate edge $s_0c$, an equivalence with inverse $s_0c$ witnessed by $s_0s_0c$. That node makes $F^\simeq\to(\Delta^0)^\simeq=\Delta^0$ a Kan fibration, so the core $K=F^\simeq$ is a Kan complex; $a$ is one of its edges by Step 4. Use generator (iv) in the square whose upper map $K^\flat\to Z$ is the inclusion and whose lower map $K^\sharp\to B$ is constant at $0$. The lower map preserves markings, and Step 2 gives a marked lift $K^\sharp\to Z$. Its underlying map is forced to be the same inclusion, because $K^\flat\to K^\sharp$ is the underlying identity. Thus $a$ is marked. In the triangle $\tau$ of Step 4, the consecutive edges $a,f'$ are now both marked. Lifting generator (iii), with upper map $\tau$ and lower map $p\tau$ into the fully marked $B$, marks the remaining long edge $f$. Again its underlying map stays $\tau$, since generator (iii) is the underlying identity.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.1.1.6(B), the core-Kan generator and consecutive-edge marking generator.

proof.text: The underlying map of $j$ now preserves every marking of $B$: its only nondegenerate edges are $[0,1],[0,2],[1,2]$, whose images are $f,h,g$, all marked. It therefore gives a marked map $s:B\to Z$ with $si=j$ and $ps=1_B$, since $pj=i$ and $i$ is the underlying identity. In the arrow category the pairs $(1_A,s):i\to j$ and $(1_A,p):j\to i$ have composite $(1_A,ps)=1_i$. Hence $i$ is a retract of $j\in W$, and the defining retract closure of $W$ proves the assertion.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.1.7; explicit arrow-category retraction after the small-object factorization.

proof_origin.place: Expanded proof of Corollary 3.1.1.7 using Remark 3.1.1.3, the forward implication of Proposition 3.1.1.6 and the opposite form of Proposition 2.4.1.7; HTT was read online and is not archived in literature/.
